comparisons.peer_topic: Definition and composition of sales and trading revenue
comparisons.peer_summary: Sales and trading revenue includes unrealized and realized gains and losses on trading assets, net interest income, and equity commissions, segregated into fixed-income, currencies, commodities, and equities.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures define the composition of trading-related revenues, but focus on different segments and structures. MS discloses that within its Wealth Management segment, trading revenues primarily stem from fixed income principal transactions and DCP investment gains/losses. In contrast, BAC discloses a broader Global Markets 'Sales and trading revenue' definition that includes unrealized/realized gains, net interest income, and equity commissions, further segmented into fixed-income, currencies, commodities, and equities. While MS highlights 'acting as principal' in fixed income within wealth management, BAC categorizes fixed-income gains/losses specifically under market making activities within its global markets scope.

sentences.text: Within the Wealth Management business segment, Trading revenues primarily include revenues from customers' purchases and sales of fixed income instruments in which we act as principal, as well as gains and losses related to DCP investments.

Sales and trading revenue includes unrealized and realized gains and losses on trading and other assets that are included in market making and similar activities, net interest income, and fees primarily from commissions on equity securities.

Sales and trading revenue is segregated into fixed-income (government debt obligations, investment and non-investment grade corporate debt obligations, commercial MBS, residential mortgage-backed securities, collateralized loan obligations, interest rate and credit derivative contracts), currencies (interest rate and foreign exchange contracts), commodities (primarily futures, forwards, swaps and options) and equities (equity-linked derivatives and cash equity activity).

comparisons.peer_summary: The increase in Fixed Income Markets revenue was driven by growth in spread products and other fixed income (up 20%), partially offset by lower revenues in rates and currencies (down 6%).
comparisons.comparison: Both companies report on Fixed Income revenue performance, but MS focuses on the internal composition of Wealth Management trading revenue while C reports on the growth drivers of its Fixed Income Markets segment. MS states that Wealth Management trading revenues primarily include revenues from customers' purchases and sales of fixed income instruments where it acts as principal. C reports that its Fixed Income Markets revenue increased, driven by growth in spread products and other fixed income (up 20%). MS details the source of revenue (principal transactions/DCP gains), whereas C details the volume/activity drivers (spread products) for its fixed income segment.

sentences.text: Within the Wealth Management business segment, Trading revenues primarily include revenues from customers' purchases and sales of fixed income instruments in which we act as principal, as well as gains and losses related to DCP investments.
The increase in Fixed Income Markets was driven by growth in spread products and other fixed income (up 20%), partially offset by lower revenues in rates and currencies (down 6%).

comparisons.peer_summary: Net revenues increased 16% to $53.51 billion in 2024, driven primarily by higher revenues in Global Banking & Markets (Equities, Investment banking, FICC) and Asset & Wealth Management (Equity investments, Management fees), with slight increases in Platform Solutions.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures discuss revenue components involving equity and fixed income activities, but in different segments. MS identifies trading revenues within Wealth Management as including gains/losses related to DCP investments and principal fixed income sales. GS reports that overall Net Revenues in 2024 were driven by higher revenues in Global Banking & Markets (including FICC and Equities) and Asset & Wealth Management (including Equity investments). While MS specifies 'DCP investments' and 'principal' fixed income sales as key trading revenue elements in Wealth Management, GS highlights 'Equity investments' and 'Management fees' as the primary drivers of growth within its Asset & Wealth Management segment.

comparisons.peer_summary: Trading liabilities increased due to client-driven market-making activities primarily in Fixed Income Markets, which resulted in higher levels of short positions in debt instruments.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures relate to Fixed Income Market-making activities and their balance sheet impact, though from different angles. MS describes Wealth Management trading revenues as including revenues from customers' purchases and sales of fixed income instruments where the company acts as principal. JPM explains that trading liabilities increased due to client-driven market-making activities primarily in Fixed Income Markets, resulting in higher short positions in debt instruments. Both identify fixed income client activity/market making as a core driver of the respective financial metrics (revenue for MS via principal roles, liabilities for JPM via short positions).
